source_text: διὸ καὶ »Ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν« καὶ ὄνομα ἔοχεν αὐτὸ δὴ τοῦτο »Μεθ᾿ »ἡμῶν ὁ θεός« ὅτε δὲ ἐδημιούργησεν, ἐπεὶ μὴ ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀποσταλεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς εἰς οὐσίαν ἔφερε τὰ πάντα, καὶ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ἦν καὶ θεὸς ἦν· λέγεται δὲ καὶ σοφία ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱός, ἀρχὴ ὁδῶν τοῦ θεοῦ κτισθεῖσα κατὰ τὴν τῶν Παροιμιῶν γραφήν, ὅτι ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ σοφία, πρὸς τὸν οὗ ἐστι σοφία ὑπάρχουαα, οὐδεμίαν σχέοιν πρὸς ἕτερόν τινα εἶχεν, ἀλλ᾿ εὐδοκία θεοῦγενόμενος τὰ κτίοματα ὑπάρξαι ἠβονλήθη. ἠθέλησεν οὖν ἀναλαβεῖν αὕτη ἡ σοφία σχέσιν δημιουργικὴν πρὸς τὰ ἐσόμενα καὶ τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ δηλούμενον διὰ τοῦ ἐκτίσθαι αὐτὴν ἀρχὴν ὁδῶν τοῦ θεοῦ, καθ᾿ ἃς ὁδοὺς διαπορεύεται οὐσιῶν διακοσμῶν προνοούμενος, εὐεργετῶν, χαριζόμενος ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ σοφίᾳ κτισθείσῃ. ἀρχὴν οὖν εἶναι τὸν λόγον φασὶν οὐχ ἕτερον ὄντα αὐτῆς κατ᾿ οὐσίαν ἀλλ᾿ ἐπινοίᾳ καὶ σγέσει, ἵν᾿ ᾖ ἡ αὐτὴ ὕπαρξις ἣν νῦν καλοῦσιν κατ᾿ οὐσίαν αἱ γραφαί, ᾗ μὲν ᾠκείωται τῷ θεῷ σοφία, ᾗ δὲ νένευκεν, ἵν᾿ οὕτως εἴπω, πρὸς τὰ δημιουργήματα ὁ δημιονργικὸς λόγος, οὐκ ἐντανῦθα δὲ μόνον ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱὸς λόγος εἴρηται· ἔστι δὲ παραθέσθαι ἡητὰ οὐκ ἐκ τῆς καινῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐκ τῆς παλαιᾶς· »Τῷ λόγῳ γὰρ κυρίου οὐρανοὶ ἐστερεώθησαν«. καὶ τὸ »Ἀπέστειλεν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰάσατο αὐτούς«. καὶ ὁ Λουκᾶς φησιν· »Καθὼς παρέδοσαν ἡμῖν οἱ ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς αὐτόπται καὶ »ὑπηρέται γενόμενοι τοῦ λόγου«.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore also He tabernacled in us, and had as name this very thing, With us God; but when he created, since not as man sent by the Father did he bring all things into substance, he was both toward God and was God. And the Son of God is also called wisdom, created beginning of ways of God according to the writing of Proverbs, because the wisdom of God, existing toward him whose wisdom she is, had no relation toward any other, but by God's good pleasure she wished the creatures to exist. So this wisdom wished to take up a creative relation toward the things that would be; and this is what is shown through her having been created beginning of ways of God, according to which ways he goes through, ordering beings, providing, benefiting, gracing, in this wisdom created. So they say the Word is beginning, not being other than her according to substance but by concept and relation, so that the same existence is what the scriptures now call according to substance: in one respect wisdom as made God's own, in another the creative Word as having inclined, so to say, toward the made things. And not here only has the Son of God been called Word; it is possible to set alongside sayings not from the new only but also from the old: For by the word of the Lord heavens were made firm. And He sent his word and healed them. And Luke says: As they handed down to us, those who from the beginning became eyewitnesses and servants of the word.
pass_b_english: That is why “he dwelt among us” (John 1:14) and had this very name, “God with us” (Matthew 1:23). But when he created, since it was not as a man sent by the Father that he brought all things into being, he was both with God and was God (John 1:1).

The Son of God is also called Wisdom, created as “the beginning of the ways” of God, according to the scripture of Proverbs (Proverbs 8:22). For the Wisdom of God, existing in relation to him whose Wisdom she is, had no relation to anything else; but by God's good pleasure she willed that created things should exist. So this Wisdom chose to take up a creative relation to the things that were to be. And this is what is meant by her being created “the beginning of the ways” of God: the ways along which he passes as he orders beings, provides for them, does them good and gives them grace, in this Wisdom that was created.

So they say that the Word is the “beginning”, not being other than Wisdom in substance, but in concept and in relation. It is one and the same existence, which the scriptures here name according to its substance: Wisdom, insofar as it belongs to God as his own; the creative Word, insofar as it has inclined, if I may put it so, toward the things that are made.

But it is not only here that the Son of God is called Word. One can set beside it sayings not only from the New Testament but also from the Old: “For by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm” (Psalm 33:6), and “He sent his word and healed them” (Psalm 107:20). And Luke says: “Just as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word handed them down to us” (Luke 1:2).
